📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin [BTC] witnessed yet another bout of volatility this week that caught the bulls off guard. On Wednesday, the 25th of November, Bitcoin bounced from a low of $57,300 to a local high of $61,622.

This bounce spurred the rest of the crypto market higher too, resulting in $406.85 million in long liquidations and $238.06 million in short liquidations.

Industry observers note that the U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data was released on Wednesday. It rose 3.8% year-over-year, while core PCE rose 3.3% year-over-year.

Headline PCE in line with consensus estimates reinforced the market expectations of a 25-bps Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

A week ago, there was a 6.5% probability of a 50-point rate hike. At the time of writing, this probability was 0%.

It wasn’t bullish news, but it was a catalyst that allowed the price to jump higher and wipe out the dense cluster of short positions that had built up in recent days. Monday’s rally just past $64k was another short squeeze.

As things stand, demand is too weak and pessimism too intense for Bitcoin to mount an immediate comeback.

Founder and CEO of intelligence platform CryptoQuant, Ki Young Ju, noted that there was $16 billion in potential short liquidations from $60k to $100k, compared to just $5 billion in potential long liquidations.

Industry observers note that in other words, a short squeeze was much more attractive in these conditions. Notably, a mini short squeeze occurred on Monday, as well as the recent price bounce back above $61k.

Sources indicate that the Bitcoin active value to investor value ratio was back near 0.8 after climbing above 1.0 earlier this year, reported a crypto analyst. Moreno. It measures how far the spot price deviates from the True Market Mean, which is the aggregate on-chain cost basis for active investors.

Readings below 1 indicate active investors are carrying losses. Aggregate profitability has deteriorated since the BTC price rebound earlier this year.

It has been revealed that the Bitcoin risk index was above 2 and neared its peak value from earlier this year. The metric reveals higher readings during sell-offs, when capital turnover intensifies relative to market value.

The two metrics showed increasing stress on the market and offered a more attractive valuation to long-term buyers.

To make a compelling case for a bullish recovery, the selling pressure needs to be absorbed. The evidence at hand does not support sizeable demand- for example, Bitcoin spot ETF flows have been overwhelmingly bearish in November.

  • MetaMask expands its payment card to Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam for Mastercard transactions.
  • Cryptocurrency wallet provider MetaMask released its payment card in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam on November 25, allowing consumers to spend its dollar-pegged mUSD stablecoin at merchants that accept Mastercard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Blitz news » MetaMask Brings Stablecoin Payments to Three Asian Markets With Upcoming Card Launch.

MetaMask expands its payment card to Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam for Mastercard transactions.

Cryptocurrency wallet provider MetaMask released its payment card in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam on November 25, allowing consumers to spend its dollar-pegged mUSD stablecoin at merchants that accept Mastercard.

In a recent development, the move gives owners in the three markets another way to use stablecoins for everyday purchases. Rather than transferring funds to a centralized cryptocurrency exchange before spending them, users can make payments directly through a card linked to their MetaMask wallet.

MetaMask Card uses mUSD, a US dollar-pegged stablecoin, to make payments at merchants that accept Mastercard. Owners can pay online with their virtual card or in stores through Apple Pay and Google Pay. At checkout, the required amount of mUSD is converted into the local currency, such as Japanese yen.

In Japan, the card is available only as a virtual version and carries no annual fee. ATM cash withdrawals are not supported. Customers can spend up to $10,000 per transaction and $15,000 per day.

Payments made with an mUSD balance at domestic merchants carry no transaction fee, while purchases at merchants outside the user’s country of residence incur a 1% fee.

To apply, users must access the Money tab in the MetaMask mobile app, register an email address and phone number, complete identity verification (KYC), and provide proof of residence.

Industry observers note that however, the card does not support direct payments with every cryptocurrency held in MetaMask. Users must first convert assets such as USDC into mUSD before adding funds to their MetaMask Money account.

The Japanese cards are issued by New Zealand-based financial services provider Immersve Limited. MetaMask notes its Money account retains a self-custodial structure, allowing customers to maintain control of their private keys.

The expansion comes as stablecoin activity continues to grow across Southeast Asia, where digital assets are increasingly used for cross-border payments and transfers.

Chainalysis’s 2026 regional research shows that Thailand and Vietnam, alongside the Philippines, accounted for 14.4% of global small-value peer-to-peer transfers. The report also found that cross-border stablecoin activity exceeded domestic volumes in both countries, reaching $10.4 billion in Thailand and $6.9 billion in Vietnam.

It has been revealed that japan offers a different opportunity. Its developing regulatory framework and growing interest in stablecoins provide another market for MetaMask to test whether crypto wallets can become practical payment tools.

MetaMask first tested its payment card in the UK and Europe in August 2024 before launching it to US customers in February 2026. The service has since expanded to the European Economic Area, Canada, and parts of Central and South America.

Zonveer ZX3 review: one of the best-value electric dirt bikes for beginners

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package.
  • It has been revealed that zonveer is a young brand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

It has been revealed that zonveer is a young brand. It debuted in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

In a recent development, A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

According to recent reports, zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

Recent findings suggest that with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

And while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Recent findings suggest that range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

Industry observers note that the sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

Industry observers note that we’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

Sources indicate that it’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

#145814. Upcoming Bitcoin Core Upgrade: Breaking Down the Details

Upcoming Bitcoin Core Upgrade: Breaking Down the Details

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The key reason behind the setup is error handling in a way where there's no break in wallet usage that needs manual intervention in the process, to a significant degree.
  • The pull request follows two earlier fixes, one for unnamed legacy wallets and another for crashes when Bitcoin Core couldn't write to the wallet directory, on the whole.
  • This isn't the first fix for wallet migration either, in the actual application.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The key reason behind the setup is error handling in a way where there's no break in wallet usage that needs manual intervention in the process, to a significant degree. Indeed, a Bitcoin wallet migration change was, broadly speaking, merged on November 25 by Bitcoin Core.

The pull request follows two earlier fixes, one for unnamed legacy wallets and another for crashes when Bitcoin Core couldn't write to the wallet directory, on the whole. In fact, the thinking is to handle failures in a controlled way so the process can (to some degree) automatically restore the original wallet without needing manual intervention.

This isn't the first fix for wallet migration either, in the actual application.

Some mismatches during wallet creation could crash the graphical app or cause it to return a generic error. Those differences are now caught by Bitcoin Core and reported, which lets the migration process restore the original wallet from its backup, There are a couple of cases where the process could abruptly stop.

Industry observers note that trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory could also throw an error and skip cleanup, in real-world scenarios. In fact, now the process crashes with a clear error message. The test for this case is checking that the wallet is still in the old database format after the failure.

The biggest change is in how Bitcoin Core moves the wallet to SQLite. Earlier, it deleted the original database before writing the new one. If something went wrong while making the new database or writing the wallet records, the user could end up restoring the backup by hand.

Now Bitcoin Core builds the SQLite database next to the original. So, the old database stays in place. These days, the new one is being built. Once the wallet records have been written successfully, Bitcoin Core can move the new database into place. The pull request also tests this with a wallet stored on a separate filesystem.

Industry observers note that A leftover SQLite journal in the wallet directory can corrupt the new database if SQLite uses it for the migrated wallet. In fact, Bitcoin Core now stops the migration when it finds a file, and the test checks that the journal stays in place. Moreover, the wallet keeps its legacy format.

It's significant to keep in mind that automatic recovery still hinges on the backup being copied back successfully. As Ryan Ofsky mentioned in his review, if that copy crashes, the user still has to restore the backup by hand, on the whole.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

In a recent development, I finally pulled my favorite fuzzy black jacket out of my closet for long strolls around Latest York City. Many of the leaves in Central Park are turning a gorgeous burnt-orange hue, and hot apple cider is readily available at local cafes and farmers' markets. But like clockwork every fall since moving to New York from Florida, my skin has been feeling dry, tight, and a little itchy. My complexion is also a little flushed after cleansing, which isn’t the norm during the spring and summer.

Turns out that I’m not alone. Dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD, claims her patients often experience rough or flaky patches, dullness, and increased sensitivity to products they previously tolerated well after cleansing this time of year. They also notice tightness, itching, and products that suddenly sting. Sure, cranking up my pretty pink Canopy humidifier can help a little, but after talking with dermatologists, it’s officially time to upgrade my skincare routine for fall.

Recent findings suggest that the good news: We don’t need to replace our entire routine this fall. Dermatologists share their ideal morning and night skincare tweaks. Plus, they reveal how to safely exfoliate dry, flaky skin, and weigh in on using retinoids. The best part? Many of their suggestions are drugstore staples from brands like Cetaphil and La Roche-Posay.

“A healthy barrier does not require a ten-product supporting cast,” indicates Dr. Gohara. You really only need a few key items—and you may even have them in your home already. Here’s a roundup of dermatologist-recommended products the pros agree are worthy of a spot in your skincare routine. I also included my favorite face sunscreen for the morning and eye cream for twice daily use.

Dr. Nazarian swears by this Cetaphil option and calls it her top cleanser because it's, well, super gentle. She highlights the trifecta of glycerin, niacinamide, and panthenol, as a major win for your skincare game. Notably, glycerin is a humectant to hold onto moisture.

Best Face Washes For Your Skin Type.

Aveeno Positively Radiant Vitamin C Serum.

According to recent reports, “Glow with a built-in comfort crew,” says Dr. Gohara about this Skincare Award-winning face serum. “Vitamin C is a proven skin-brightening, collagen-boosting powerhouse. The only problem: it’s known to be irritating on sensitive skin. Aveeno has solved for that here, adding a calming concoction of niacinamide and the brand’s famed oat complex,” says beauty director Brian Underwood.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve previously named this the best overall hyaluronic acid serum and Dr. Nazarian agrees. She appreciates that it boasts multiple forms of hyaluronic acid to enhance hydration, adding that it’s a great serum for layering with other products in your routine.

Aquaphor Hydrating Daily Lotion.

Industry observers note that you can slather this budget-friendly moisturizer on your face and body. It earned snaps from Dr. Gohara, who points to the combination of glycerin to attract water and ceramides to support the skin barrier.

In a recent development, pro tip from Dr. Gohara: Whether you use a lotion or a face cream, apply it to slightly damp skin.

SkinMedica Barrier Calming Cream.

Recent findings suggest that for extra dryness, layer SkinMedica Barrier Calming Cream on top, advises Dr. Gohara. “Just as you double up on clothes, you can double up on moisturizer. Hydration first, a protective outer layer second,” she says. And that’s exactly what the Barrier Calming Cream does. It contains a nourishing blend of moisturizing glycerin, niacinamide to minimize skin inflammation, and calming oat kernel extract.

According to recent reports, the experts I chatted with say eye cream is a totally optional step. You can technically get away with just using a plain face moisturizer under your eyes, states Dr. Nazarian. However, since the undereye skin is thinner and prone to dryness during colder months, a separate eye cream can be helpful for dealing with dryness, fine lines, or crepiness.

In a recent development, neocutis combines human growth factors with a proprietary blend of peptides to target fine lines, wrinkles, puffiness, and dark circles. After about two weeks, I noticed my undereye area was a little more luminous.

Isdin Eryfotona Actinica Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50+.

You shouldn’t retire your sunscreen in the fall, argues Dr. Gohara. A broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher sunscreen is a daily staple. My all-time favorite one is the Isdin Eryfotona Ageless—it’s a tinted mineral sunscreen that doesn’t leave a ghastly finish on my face. It contains plankton-derived DNA Repairsomes, which Isdin says help repair existing sun damage. The formulation is lightweight and absorbs quickly and it’s even water-resistant for active lifestyles.

SkinMedica HA5 Hydra Collagen Facial Mist.

Industry observers note that spritz your skin with this spray whenever your complexion needs extra TLC. Dr. Gohara calls this your skin’s “hydration intermission.” It moisturizes and helps keep water in, and layers beautifully over makeup.

Before you go to bed and watch TV, you’ll want to do your skincare routine. You can use pretty much everything from your morning routine.

This creamy cleanser is great for seasonal dryness.

Industry observers note that pro tip from Dr. Garshick: Avoid washing with very hot water since it can contribute to dryness. If you have very sensitive skin, consider splashing your face with water instead of cleansing twice daily, she says.

Industry observers note that "This eye cream is rich without being heavy so it won’t leave skin with an oily finish,” states dermatologist Joshua Zeichner, MD, in our 2020 Skincare Awards. He loves that it can “help strengthen the skin and improve texture and fine lines—no irritation in sight.".

Lock in hydration with this lightweight face serum that doesn’t feel overly tacky on your skin.

SkinMedica makes a slew of impressive products, including a recent 2026 Skincare Award win for the Exfoliating Pads. However, when you’re shopping for a moisturizer for fall, consider this investment-worthy pick. While pricey, you only need a few small dabs of cream all over your face.

Dr. Nazarian suggests Dermal Repair Cream to anyone who wants to use a retinoid product in the fall. “It’s incredibly hydrating and calming—and uses a form of hyaluronic acid combined with vitamins C and E for skin hydration and environmental defense along with a gentle form of retinoid,” she says. Just be sure to gradually introduce it into your routine.

In the fall, it’s all about hydration. Both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Nazarian suggest humectants such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid to attract water, plus skin barrier-supporting ingredients such as ceramides. You might also benefit from slathering on a richer cream packed with fatty acids, shea butter, or squalane if your skin is very dry.

Sources indicate that yes, you can exfoliate in the fall, but only occasionally. TBH, the frequency varies based on your specific needs and the product you’re using. But you can probably start with once a week or even every two weeks if you have more sensitive skin. You should also avoid scrubbing irritated skin and not exfoliate the same night you use a retinoid while building tolerance. “Flakes are not an invitation to scrub harder,” says Dr. Gohara. “You are polishing skin, not refinishing furniture.” Also, don't be afraid to pause exfoliating if your skin ever feels uncomfy. You can just use your classic face moisturizer until your skin feels comfortable again, adds Dr. Gohara.

Look, just because it’s overcast and chilly out doesn’t mean you should skip wearing sunscreen in the fall. And don’t just take my word for it: “Your sweaters have seasonal employment; your sunscreen works year-round,” says Dr. Gohara. That means you should wear a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher on your exposed skin, including your ears, neck, and hands. Follow your sunscreen label for specific reapplication tips, but typically, you can reapply at least every two hours and after sweating or swimming, according to the American Academy of Dermatology.

The experts I spoke with say you can use a retinoid year-round if your skin can tolerate it and if you diligently reapply sunscreen. However, fall is a convenient time to add a retinoid—such as retinol, retinal, tretinoin, or adapalene—into your routine. Regardless of which type of retinoid you select, start using it gradually. Dr. Garshick states two or three times a week is a good jumping off point, then you can increase frequency as tolerated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crypto has an AI sector of its own, and from the outside it looks like one trade. Up close, the projects in it do very different jobs, and a comparison only makes sense once you know which job each one does.

Recent findings suggest that part of the sector already earns real revenue. Venice, a private AI app, became a unicorn in July 2026 with a $65 million Series A, and its CEO, Erik Voorhees, told TechCrunch that the organization is profitable, with annualized run-rate revenues of over $70 million. People pay for private AI.

The map goes layer by layer, and each project is described from its own site.

The base layer connects idle graphics cards with the people who need them.

It has been revealed that most of what this layer sells is time on hardware, though Akash and io.net now also sell access to open models through APIs. For teams weighing a rented GPU against their own hardware, Lightchain AI has published a comparison of self-hosting an LLM and a worker network.

Here the network itself decides whose work is best, and pays for it.

This layer competes with ChatGPT on the user’s side of the screen.

Lightchain is building an agents layer of its own, Lightchain Agents, with a waitlist open now.

This is where Lightchain AI sits. It is a layer-1 blockchain built to run AI. Its blog keeps a plain list of what is live on the network today.

Lightchain also touches three of the other layers:.

Recent findings suggest that the sector will keep trading as one theme. It works more like a stack, where each layer needs the others: GPUs to run on, models worth running, apps people want, agents that act, and a record that shows what happened. Lightchain’s bet is on that last layer: the more AI runs on open networks, and the more agents pay one another, the more a public record of who served each answer matters.

Lightchain AI is a layer-1 blockchain for AI. Independent operators stake LCAI and serve open models such as gpt-oss, Qwen3, and Llama from their own GPUs. The chain assigns each job, holds the fee in escrow, and keeps a record of every job that anyone can look up. Products live today include Lightchain Chat, Lightchain Desktop (beta), Lightchain Studio, the Lightchain Bridge, and the Lightscan explorer. The LCAI DUNA, a Wyoming association, is the project’s legal entity.

Website: lightchain.ai · X: @LightchainAI · Discord: discord.gg/lightchain.

Coinbase has suspended trading for 12 crypto trading pairs, including those of Cardano (ADA) and Stellar (XLM), as November 2026 wraps up with just a few days left.

The delisting took place on November 25, as Coinbase declared earlier. The affected pairs include APE-USDT, ATOM-USDT, ALGO-BTC, CRV-BTC, ETC-BTC, XLM-BTC, ICP-BTC, and ADA-ETH, among others.

The full list includes APE-USDT, ATOM-USDT, ALGO-BTC, CRV-BTC, ETC-BTC, ICP-BTC, XLM-BTC, APE-EUR, ADA-ETH, 1INCH-GBP, CHZ-GBP, and SNX-GBP, with trading suspended across Coinbase Exchange, Advanced Trade and Coinbase Prime.

Coinbase regularly monitors the markets on the exchange and, in an effort to improve overall market health and consolidate liquidity, has removed a number of non-USD trading pairs for supported assets.

Sources indicate that in similar delisting news, Coinbase has disabled trading for Stargate Finance (STG), Vulcan Forged (PYR), Neon EVM (NEON), and Syndicate (SYND), in line with the shake-up on its platform in November. Users' funds will remain accessible, and users will be able to withdraw them at any time.

As stated earlier, Coinbase regularly monitors the markets on the exchange and might delist some assets to improve overall market health and consolidate liquidity.

According to recent reports, based on recent reviews, Coinbase will suspend trading for Centrifuge (CFG) on December 18, 2026, at or around 2 PM ET. Centrifuge has separately declared it is ending token support for CFG and allowing holders to convert CFG tokens into equity in Centrifuge.

According to recent reports, also in December, Coinbase will be performing a system upgrade. In an X post, the exchange stated it has scheduled a system upgrade for Saturday, December 5, 2026, around 7 a.m. PT, estimated to last about 4 hours.

During this time, Coinbase stated that all trading and transfers will be unavailable, and the Coinbase Exchange will be temporarily offline. Users are advised to take note and prepare accordingly so as to avoid any delays on that date.

Breaking: Tesla kills $41,990 Model Y AWD: all-wheel drive now costs $8,000 more

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator.
  • The trim lasted just over nine months.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

When Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

Recent findings suggest that and the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

In a recent development, add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

The timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

In a recent development, if you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a upcoming Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

In a recent development, this is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent new Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

It has been revealed that we liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

It has been revealed that now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

According to recent reports, there are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

In a recent development, tesla is not going to keep 6 different model Y trims especially when the most expensive trim in the Model YL is selling. They will definitely squeeze out as much money from selling more expensive trims so the lowest end trim will most likely be next to go.

And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

According to recent reports, that’s a problem for a tech giant whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

Two XRP Ledger lending amendments, LendingProtocol and LendingProtocolV1_1, each have 28 votes out of 35 validators, or 80%, according to XRPScan data on Thursday. Each of them needs one more vote to start a 14-day countdown to activation, according to XRPScan.

On Wednesday, the SingleAssetVault amendment reached 29 votes. According to XRPScan, its earliest activation date is Dec. 9, and its support has to stay above 80% until then.

XRP was trading at around $0.95 on Thursday, up 4.1% over 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap.

On Nov. 20, XRPScan indicated 25 votes for SingleAssetVault and 24 votes for each of the two lending amendments. Validators run by Interledger, onXRP, GateHub and Flare were among the last to vote for them.

Industry observers note that rippleX opened LendingProtocolV1_1 for voting with a post on X on Sept. 30, when the amendment arrived with rippled version 3.4.0. "LendingProtocolV1_1 is open for validator voting. It introduces closed-ended vaults and cash-basis accounting for XRPL lending, and it must activate before LendingProtocol and SingleAssetVault can proceed," the RippleX developer account wrote.

Sources indicate that J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, explained the role of the update in a post on June 25. "v1.1 is an enhancement to the Lending Protocol, not a replacement for v1.0," he wrote, adding that "Lending on XRPL will evolve dynamically.".

In a recent development, ripple described the mechanics of the protocol on Nov. 19. "The upcoming XRP Ledger Lending Protocol is designed to bring loan issuance and repayment directly onto the ledger. Lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital to glitch loans and track repayments onchain," the organization wrote on X.

Ripple engineer Ed Hennis presented the protocol in a thread on X in December 2025. He called it a protocol-native system for "fixed-term, fixed-rate, underwritten credit." "XRP's $124B market cap can finally be lent into institutional credit facilities to generate real yield instead of sitting idle," Hennis wrote at the time.

According to recent reports, jazzi Cooper, head of product at RippleX, wrote on Sept. 11 that "XRP as collateral for institutional credit is a killer use case (and supported by xls65/66 lending protocol!)".

On the same day, the XRP Ledger Foundation shared an interview with its chief technology officer, Denis Angell. "We are writing TradFi primitives into the XRP Ledger," Angell stated. In the interview, he compared the lending protocol to a closed-end fund, where investors put in XRP or RLUSD and receive interest.

Bitcoin miners lose hashrate as hackers hijack up to 1,600 sites

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (463 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the 25th of November, Bitcoin mining manufacturer Braiins warned that attackers had hijacked Bitcoin miners’ work through unencrypted pool connections.
  • According to recent reports, machines kept running while someone else received credit.
  • Recent findings suggest that its investigation documented four episodes on the 20th of November, mostly in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the 25th of November, Bitcoin mining manufacturer Braiins warned that attackers had hijacked Bitcoin miners’ work through unencrypted pool connections.

According to recent reports, machines kept running while someone else received credit. That basically left operators paying electricity bills for work credited elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that its investigation documented four episodes on the 20th of November, mostly in Europe. Each affected 1,050–1,600 mining sites and diverted 0.6–1.9 EH/s for six to 49 minutes.

Attackers forged internet routing announcements, known as BGP hijacking, to intercept connections and impersonate the pool. Miners reconnected to the same address, making the switch difficult to spot.

Earlier episodes hit Latin America between the 7th and 12th of November.

Sources indicate that responding to an X user, Braiins noted the attacks exploited a weakness in Stratum V1, the protocol connecting miners to pools. Stratum V2 contributor Pavlenex added,.

This is an attack on MINERS and their infrastructure and is not a vulnerability in Braiins Pool.

The exposed protocol dates back to 2012, and warnings have been issued for years.

According to recent reports, braiins had flagged hashrate theft on the 18th of April 2020. It argued that preventing stolen revenue and reducing operating expenses would encourage upgrades more effectively than decentralization alone.

That history prompted Turtlecute, who works in product marketing at Braiins, to write,.

For 14 years, we ignored SV1 challenges.

When an X user asked whether this was the first publicly confirmed case, Pavlenex recalled earlier reports of interception attacks.

It has been revealed that by November, the financial incentive for upgrading had become harder to dismiss. Braiins reported that miners’ machines showed normal activity while their pool dashboards recorded no credited hashrate.

It has been revealed that six months earlier, seven mining organizations had joined the Stratum V2 Working Group. These included ANTPOOL, Foundry, F2Pool, SpiderPool, Block, MARA Foundation, and DMND.

Reportedly, the organizations represented roughly 75% of the global hashrate at the time. Their backing gave the encrypted replacement substantial reach, but deployment remained uneven.

As of the 26th of November, the official directory listed Braiins Pool and DMND as production pools. It separately listed several solo pools and MARA Foundation’s industrial solo operation.

Industry observers note that foundry remained marked as work in progress, despite reported testing in November. ANTPOOL, F2Pool, and SpiderPool were absent from the production listings.

Recent findings suggest that the exposure extended beyond V2 adoption. Braiins mentioned most major pools’ public endpoints still offered only unencrypted Stratum V1 during its checks on the 23rd of November.

Pools, Miners, fix your URLs today.

V2 encrypts mining traffic and verifies the pool’s identity, preventing an impersonator from receiving miners’ work. The November attacks demonstrated the revenue consequences when industry support had yet to reach those connections.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.
  • Sources indicate that the second major trucking deal between Facebook parent firm Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 upcoming battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

Sources indicate that the second major trucking deal between Facebook parent firm Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 upcoming battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

“Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, stated Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

Meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The company adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy latest trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

It has been revealed that yuck. That's the feeling I get when reading this. Am I happy that more EV semi's will be going on the road? Yes. But the way it's being done just makes me feel dirty. And I refuse to do or have anything that Mark Zuckerberg is involved with. I find him to be disgusting. But then again I find most of these super wealthy people to be vomit inducing.

So I'd liken this deal to a guy who goes out to a bar with the sole intention of "having some fun". And it doesn't matter to him how that happens, as long as he gets his happy ending. But then when the sun rises and the darkness vanishes, who this guy slept with is revealed and it's not good.

Zucherberg isn't doing any of this for the planet. He's doing it for money.

Nevoya expects Meta’s fresh batch of semis to begin prowling I-10 in 2027, where they’ll cover approximately 4 million freight miles annually.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • XRP has seen traders withdraw large amounts of tokens out of major crypto exchanges, especially Binance, over the last 30 days even as the broad market volatility persists.
  • Despite the intense selling pressure XRP has witnessed over the past few months, data from the crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant demonstrates that XRP’s exchange outflow has reached 5 billion XRP over the last month.
  • While the massive 30-day exchange outflow of 5 billion XRP is a relief signal because it signals persistent demand for XRP even amid the intense volatility, further data shows that the outflow is relatively low compared to levels seen in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP has seen traders withdraw large amounts of tokens out of major crypto exchanges, especially Binance, over the last 30 days even as the broad market volatility persists.

Despite the intense selling pressure XRP has witnessed over the past few months, data from the crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant demonstrates that XRP’s exchange outflow has reached 5 billion XRP over the last month.

While the massive 30-day exchange outflow of 5 billion XRP is a relief signal because it signals persistent demand for XRP even amid the intense volatility, further data shows that the outflow is relatively low compared to levels seen in October.

Although the 5 billion XRP outflow is significant and November has yet to wrap up, the data indicates that it marks a decent decrease from October, when total exchange outflows for the month reached about 5.7 billion XRP.

Despite the 700,000 XRP decrease in the metric, the outflows registered in the last 30 days are still considered substantial and have drawn attention from market analysts as they signal strong investor conviction even as XRP suffered larger price losses this month compared with October.

Usually, increases in the exchange outflow of an asset suggest that investors are moving assets off exchanges into external wallets, most likely to hold them for longer periods.

Hence, this metric provides a bullish signal for XRP as it indicates strong demand among traders, putting Binance in the spotlight as over a billion XRP were withdrawn from the exchange during the period.

While OKX and Bybit saw traders withdraw 865.27 million XRP and 697.65 million XRP from their platforms, respectively, Binance registered the highest XRP withdrawals, with about 1.439 billion XRP leaving its exchange over the period.

#145800. Your Guide to Running on the Treadmill This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2294 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Your Guide to Running on the Treadmill This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there’s almost no other cardio machine that brings up as many feelings as the treadmill.
  • According to recent reports, then, last winter happened.
  • In a recent development, but, as any treadmill hater knows, moving a run indoors isn’t as simple as it sounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there’s almost no other cardio machine that brings up as many feelings as the treadmill. For the first few years of my running career, I’d do just about everything I could to avoid hopping on one, even if that meant running in freezing temps or heavy rain.

According to recent reports, then, last winter happened. There was more snow and ice on the ground in Latest York City than I had seen in a long time, but I had a half-marathon to train for. It left me no choice: I had to move my workouts to the treadmill unless I wanted to end up like that meme where the woman says snow is the perfect texture for running just to wipe out on live television a few seconds later.

In a recent development, but, as any treadmill hater knows, moving a run indoors isn’t as simple as it sounds. A lot changes on a tread—form, mental stimulation, pace—and it can totally mess with your head. Once you understand why, though, it’s a lot easier to work with the treadmill instead of against it; here’s how.

Industry observers note that because it is! For starters, your form changes. “Many people shorten their stride on the treadmill—me included,” indicates Amy Woods, a USAT-certified run coach and ISSA-certified strength and conditioning coach. “We also tend to run a little more upright.”.

Sources indicate that there’s a simple reason behind it. When you’re running outside, your legs have all the space they need for each stride, but on a treadmill, you’re contained to the length and width of the belt. Plus, most people tend to stick too close to the front of the tread, making their space even smaller, indicates Morgan Mowers, PT, DPT, a physical therapist and V.02-certified run coach.

Sources indicate that between a shortened stride and the fact that it’s a bit easier to propel yourself forward when you’ve got the help of the moving belt, you end up using different muscles on a treadmill compared to outdoors. “We see a decrease in activation of hamstrings and glutes, those bigger propellers that push you forward,” Mowers says. Instead, you’re seeing more activation in your hip flexors, quads, calves, and knees.

Recent findings suggest that on paper, a lot of these differences should actually make treadmill running easier than running outside. Another example? A treadmill provides a consistent surface. Outside, terrain and incline can vary with each step, so you call on more stabilizing muscles in your ankles and calves, Mowers says. “With every step, there's a little bit of a change when you're running outside versus on a treadmill,” she says. “Even if you are changing up the incline, it's the same exact surface over and over again.” You also don’t have to deal with the same environmental challenges—like heat and wind resistance—that come with running outside. There’s even a famous 1996 study that claims runners should set their incline to 1 percent to accommodate for the difference.

Even with all these easier-sounding differences, running on a treadmill often feels anything but. For many people, myself included, slowing down on a treadmill is the norm. One possible reason: You may just not be used to it, Woods states. Running safely on a treadmill, especially at higher speeds, takes practice. “It's definitely a different feeling when you're running on a treadmill,” Woods says. “You have to be more aware of your foot placement, your arm swing, and where your eyes are looking.” Even if you’re not consciously aware of it, your proprioception (your ability to sense your body’s position in space) could be affected.

Plus, when you’re on the treadmill, you’re stuck at one pace unless you change it, Mowers points out. “That consistency that your body is feeling on a treadmill can make it feel harder, and also may result in you going at an overall slower pace,” she claims. When you hop on a treadmill, you start yourself at a pace and settle in until you physically change it. Over the course of a mile outdoors, in comparison, you may start at an 11:00 pace, then speed up to a 10:45 pace for most of it, and end up cruising at a 10:30 pace—all without really noticing. Even though your effort feels the same, your outdoor mile ends up faster.

In a recent development, then there’s the mental side of things. Outside, you’ve got much more stimulation, states Rachelle Reed, PhD, an exercise physiologist. Your surroundings can offer the perfect distraction, and the natural variations in scenery, incline, terrain, and pace can help keep your brain more engaged too. This can have an impact on your rate of perceived exertion (RPE), Reed says. In fact, a 2019 meta-analysis found that at faster speeds, runners rated their effort as harder on a treadmill compared to outdoors. Basically, it’s harder to go hard on the tread. And because running on a treadmill is technically easier than running outdoors because you have less variation, wind resistance, and environmental factors to navigate at any given moment, that higher RPE really speaks to the mental effects of being inside, Reed says.

It has been revealed that the good news? All these differences between treadmill and outdoor running only really matter if you’re training for a race. That’s because come race day, you’ll want your muscles fully prepped to accommodate your outdoor stride, along with the ability to run across inconsistent terrain and in various elements, Mowers says. Meanwhile, if you’re just looking to do cardio, you can take your pick between the two.

If you are in fact training for a race, how should a treadmill fit into your training? In this case, going outside tends to be superior to staying in, our experts agree. Don’t move your run to the tread at just any sign of inconvenience—running in the rain, cold, and (reasonable) heat all make you a better runner, and you never know if those conditions will pop up on race day, so you’ll be glad to have the practice.

Still, there are definitely situations where it’s not a good idea to go outside. Mowers draws the line when it comes to safety: If the ground is icy, snowy, or slippery in any way, she’ll stay inside to avoid potential injury. If temps are dangerously hot, she’ll run on the treadmill. If there’s risk from serious weather, like thunder and lightning or flooding, she’ll also stay safe indoors. And, she’ll stick to her tread in the event of poor air quality (anything that’s an air quality index over 101).

It has been revealed that it’s always worth considering personal safety, too. If your only window to run is late at night and you feel more comfortable staying indoors, do that.

How hot is too hot? This is going to vary down to the person and place. Anything above 85 degrees can be dangerous, Woods says, and you also need to factor in dew point, humidity, and the effort of your run. (Harder efforts are more risky than easier ones.) If temps are higher and you decide to run outdoors, make sure you bring plenty of hydration and fuel, go slower than normal, and pay attention to signs of overheating.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also the convenience factor. You may need to do a run on the treadmill because it’s more accommodating to your schedule or childcare needs. That’s totally okay too. Ideally, the majority of your runs (we’re talking about 80 percent, and especially your long runs) will be outside, but if you’re someone who finds themselves needing to do the bulk of their running indoors, a run coach can help you make sure you’re prepped for race day. (Woods works with athletes who do the bulk of their training on treads—it’s possible!) The treadmill exists for a reason, and your training will not be affected by the occasional indoor run.

According to recent reports, first and foremost, don’t be too hard on yourself about pace. “I always disconnect from pace on the treadmill,” Woods claims. Instead, she focuses on her time and RPE. It’s really about thinking about the “spirit of the workout,” she says. For example, you can pay attention to what heart rate zone or effort level you’re supposed to get to and match that—even if that looks slower and feels harder indoors.

And, no, you don’t need to set your incline to 1 percent to compensate for bringing your workout indoors, our experts agree. The biggest reason? The study that established the idea was very small (it had just nine participants) and done only in men. That said, the incline buttons will become useful depending on the kind of run you have on deck for the day.

In a recent development, finally, give yourself a good warm-up on the treadmill, Mowers says. “Just the act of getting on a treadmill is going to increase our heart rate a little bit because we're a hamster on a wheel; we're trying not to fall off of this thing, and we're so aware of the fact that we're running,” she says. You may need at least 10 to 15 minutes to settle in before getting started with the rest of your workout.

Here’s how to approach different kinds of runs indoors.

Industry observers note that nothing really has to change, Woods says. It may take you a little longer to run a 5K on your treadmill, but try to stick to the appropriate lower heart rate zones and RPE that you’d normally achieve on these kinds of runs outdoors.

Industry observers note that you can play with incline if you’d like—but it’s not a requirement if this is a one-off run you’re doing inside. Running for one day on a completely flat surface won’t affect your training. One reason you may want to try changing the incline may simply be because it adds some variety and stimulation, Woods notes. If you’re someone who struggles because the treadmill feels boring, try increasing the incline anywhere from 1 to 4 percent for anywhere from 30 seconds to a few minutes every so often.

In a recent development, another hack: Every 10 minutes, increase your speed slightly. That should give you enough time to warm up a little each time and settle into the pace, so you shouldn’t see much of a jump in demand on your heart rate or effort.

This one gets a bit trickier, Woods says. Going at all-out speeds on a treadmill can be much tougher—and not feel super safe. This is a time when you’ll want to think about the spirit of the workout. If you have intervals where you’re supposed to get to max heart rate efforts, instead of turning up the speed super high, you can increase the incline in addition to adjusting the speed slightly, Woods says. That should still get you to your zone 4 or 5, all while allowing you to stay slower and feel more in control. This is much easier to accomplish in a tempo run (where you’re holding the pace for longer chunks of time) compared to intervals, so you could also swap an interval run for tempo too.

According to recent reports, you also have the option to skip a speed workout, Woods states. Missing one session won’t have an impact on your training, and if you’d rather not do it on the treadmill, you also have the option to switch it with another run for the week.

Sources indicate that now, here’s a workout that translates pretty well to the treadmill: All you have to do is up your incline for the duration marked in your workout. Woods recommends sticking between 1 and 4 percent as a good rule of thumb, but you can always bump up to 5 to 8 as long as you can keep good run form.

Ideally, you can move your long run to another day when you can run outside. But, if not, go by time—not mileage. Woods doesn’t recommend running on a treadmill for longer than two hours unless you are very experienced on one because of how it affects your form.

Sources indicate that you also have the option to break up your run and do 90 minutes in the morning and 90 minutes in the afternoon. “This will help with form deterioration which is more noticeable and can be more dangerous on a tread,” Woods states.

While you’re on your long run, you’ll also want to incorporate moments of incline running and even some pace variation—both for improving your running and also giving yourself a mental reset. Woods also loves to sprinkle in 15- to 30-second walking breaks every mile or so to reset her form and hydrate.

In a recent development, then the world is really your oyster on the treadmill, but all the same ideas apply: Focus on time and effort, not pace. And, feel free to sprinkle in different inclines and speeds to work different heart rate zones and find moments of mental reset.

Olivia Luppino is an associate editor at Women’s Health. She reports, writes, and edits content ranging from service stories to in-depth features and awards packages across all verticals, including health, fitness, sports, and beauty. While at WH, she’s traveled to Paris, France to watch Faith Kipyegon attempt a sub-4-minute mile and covered major races like Ultra Trail du Mont Blanc in Chamonix. Olivia is a RRCA-certified running coach who is especially passionate about helping people start their running journey and is training for her second marathon. Her works also appears in New York Magazine’s The Cut, PS (formerly Popsugar), and Salon, where she also did on-camera interviews with celebrity guests.

#145798. Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2052 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase.
  • Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
  • LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the firm has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting fresh gear.

Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the firm has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

The fresh S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

According to recent reports, the other big piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

Recent findings suggest that GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

In a recent development, perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re massive, but removing them is doable.

GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.

There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.

According to recent reports, the clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.

Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.

Industry observers note that there’s an important caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T indicates it is presently fundraising, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.

So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a manufacturer to watch.

Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.

And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).

The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.

Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.

Recent findings suggest that real Motors looks to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.

The organization has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.

I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!

Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock tech giant for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.

Industry observers note that now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The organization revealed off its fresh Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.

In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.

The organization also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.

Both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.

At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.

There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.

The fresh models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.

With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.

Yamaha highlighted off its new NMAX E electric scooter, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.

Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the new model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.

The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s fresh compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.

With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.

Segway demonstrated off a fresh vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.

Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.

The concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.

Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.

With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.

In a recent development, the firm revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.

With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.

NIU showed off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.

The company showed off several new models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.

While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push upcoming tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the company has been known for.

For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.

Industry observers note that with its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up new possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.

Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely fresh types of riding experiences.

While the bike remains a design concept with no revealed production aims, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.

Vespa highlighted off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.

A latest Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.

The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The U.S. House Financial Services Committee has advanced H.R. 8957, known as the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, bringing the proposed legislation one step closer to a full House vote.

According to recent reports, introduced on the 21st of May 2026 by Republican Representative Nick Begich of Alaska, alongside Democratic Representative Jared Golden, the bill seeks to give the U.S. government’s Strategic Bitcoin [BTC] Reserve a formal legal foundation.

Recent findings suggest that it proposes that the U.S. Treasury Department establish two separate structures within 180 days of the legislation becoming law. This includes a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve exclusively for Bitcoin and a Digital Asset Stockpile for other cryptocurrencies held by the federal government.

Under the proposal, Bitcoin owned by the federal government through criminal or civil asset forfeitures and other qualifying sources would be transferred to the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.

Here, the most significant provision is a 20-year minimum holding requirement, which would prevent the government from selling, swapping, auctioning, or using reserve Bitcoin as collateral during that period. At the same time, the bill also allows the Treasury Department to explore budget-neutral ways of acquiring additional Bitcoin without increasing the national debt.

In a recent development, separately, the legislation proposes a Digital Asset Stockpile to manage other cryptocurrencies held by the federal government. Lastly, it also introduces requirements for transparency, auditing, and congressional reporting to ensure proper oversight of these assets.

According to recent reports, the bill is particularly significant because it seeks to give the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve a statutory foundation. For its part, President Donald Trump had already established the reserve through an executive order in March 2025.

However, H.R. 8957 aims to formalize its structure and introduce additional safeguards, including the proposed 20-year holding period.

It has been revealed that as of now, twenty months have already passed, and the U.S. government reportedly holds around 328,000 BTC, largely from seizures and forfeitures, while governments globally hold about 435,000 BTC.

Henceforth, if H.R. 8957 becomes law, the reserve would receive statutory backing, making it more difficult for a future administration to reverse the policy unilaterally.

The bill received approval from the House Financial Services Committee on 16th September 2026 in a 28-21 vote, with all Republican members voting in favor and all Democratic members opposing it.

Recent findings suggest that then, on the 24th of November, the committee formally reported the revised legislation to the full House, placing it on the Union Calendar and making it eligible for a floor vote. However, its chances of becoming law remain uncertain.

This is because the 119th Congress ends on the 3rd of January 2027, leaving limited time for the bill to pass the House, clear the Senate, and receive presidential approval.

In a recent development, adding to this, market expectations also remain pessimistic, with Polymarket traders assigning only a 4% probability to the U.S. establishing a national Bitcoin reserve through legislation before 2027.

All of this coincided with Bitcoin trading at $60,355.92 at press time after a hike of 2.1% in the past 24 hours.

Hyundai is skipping the typical mid-cycle refresh and plans to launch a completely redesigned Kona, with a sleek upcoming style and an updated high-tech interior.

It’s been nearly four years since Hyundai introduced the second-generation Kona, meaning, like most of its models, the compact SUV was expected to receive a mid-cycle refresh.

Recent findings suggest that hyundai is apparently going straight to the third-generation model instead. Earlier this year, early-stage prototypes were spotted in Korea that looked much boxier and more rugged than the current Kona.

Since then, several test mules have been captured testing in the US, Europe, and other regions, confirming the Kona will adopt a more upright, traditional SUV design similar to the fresh Santa Fe, Palisade, and Tucson.

The wider, more powerful design appears to draw inspiration from Hyundai’s off-road Crater Concept, revealed at the LA Auto Show last year.

Sources indicate that hyundai mentioned the off-road SUV Concept was a preview of the “next evolution” of its Extreme Rugged Terrain (XRT) vehicles, such as the IONIQ 5 XRT and Palisade XRT Pro. Is the Kona next in line to receive the XRT treatment?

A post shared by SHORTS CAR (@shorts_car).

Apparent leaked images from a few months ago revealed a design that looked like a mashup of the Crater Concept and IONIQ 5, with pixelated lighting and a clamshell hood.

Most recently, the third-gen Hyundai Kona, codenamed “SX3,” was spotted disguised in a parking garage in Korea. The images were sent to ShortsCar, revealing the newly introduced Kona’s wheel design.

While earlier reports suggested Hyundai planned to drop the all-electric Kona variant and would only offer gas and hybrid versions, the prototype captured in Korea is expected to be the EV model. However, Hyundai has yet to confirm powertrain or battery specs.

The updates are even more evident on the inside. Previous spy images appeared to show the third-gen Hyundai Kona running Hyundai’s latest Pleos Connect infotainment system, like the IONIQ 3.

In the IONIQ 3, Hyundai offers a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Like the current model, the third-gen Kona is expected to be available with fully electric (EV), hybrid, and gas-powered powertrains.

While Hyundai skipped the 2026 Kona EV, the electric version could return in 2027 or 2028 when the third-generation model is expected to arrive.

The hybrid version will likely use the same 1.6L hybrid engine as the new Seltos, while the EV variant could offer similar powertrain and battery options to the IONIQ 3.

The IONIQ 3 is available with two battery packs in Europe and the UK: 42 kWh and 61 kWh, offering WLTP ranges of up to 213 miles (344 km) and 308 miles (497 km), respectively.
