💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin's recovery above $60,000 faces a fresh test from Japan's inflation report while US spot Bitcoin ETFs remain closed for Thanksgiving.
  • Industry observers note that the flagship cryptocurrency fell to $57,210 on Wednesday before recovering to close at $60,368, according to CryptoSlate's data.
  • However, the recovery comes as Bank of Japan officials signal that further monetary tightening may be necessary to contain inflation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin's recovery above $60,000 faces a fresh test from Japan's inflation report while US spot Bitcoin ETFs remain closed for Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that the flagship cryptocurrency fell to $57,210 on Wednesday before recovering to close at $60,368, according to CryptoSlate's data. Bitcoin extended those gains modestly on Thursday, trading around $60,538 as of 10:40 UTC.

However, the recovery comes as Bank of Japan officials signal that further monetary tightening may be necessary to contain inflation.

Speaking in Yamanashi on Thursday, BOJ board member Naoki Tamura said the central bank could accelerate interest rate increases if underlying inflation shows signs of exceeding its 2% target.

According to recent reports, tamura also reaffirmed his estimate that Japan's neutral interest rate, the level at which monetary policy neither stimulates nor restrains economic activity, stands at around 2%. That is 75 basis points above the BOJ's current overnight policy rate of 1.25%, which the central bank maintained at its October meeting.

In a recent development, the yen strengthened modestly on Thursday, with BOJ data showing the dollar trading around 159.17 yen at 5 p.m. in Tokyo, compared with 159.21 earlier in the day.

Markets will get a fresh read on Japan's inflation trajectory when Tokyo publishes its preliminary November consumer price figures at 8:30 a.m. local time on Friday, equivalent to 6:30 p.m. ET on Thanksgiving.

In a recent development, the release precedes Japan's nationwide inflation report on Dec. 18, giving investors an earlier opportunity to reassess expectations for BOJ monetary policy.

That timing leaves Bitcoin exposed to changes in those expectations before US spot ETFs resume trading during Friday's shortened NYSE Arca session.

Japan's monetary tightening poses two distinct risks to investors who borrowed yen to finance positions in Bitcoin and other dollar-denominated assets.

The strategy, commonly known as the yen carry trade, involves borrowing in Japan's relatively low-interest-rate currency and deploying the proceeds into assets elsewhere in pursuit of higher returns.

A strengthening yen increases the dollar cost of repaying that debt for investors who have not hedged their currency exposure, eroding returns even when Bitcoin's price remains unchanged.

Higher Japanese interest rates compound that pressure by potentially increasing the cost of refinancing existing positions.

Together, those developments can make leveraged investments less profitable, encouraging traders to reduce exposure to risk assets to repay their yen-denominated liabilities.

The cost of a yen-funded position can rise even if Bitcoin’s dollar price holds steady.

Currency and refinancing costs can rise separately or together.

Actual costs depend on the loan and currency hedge.

The diagram separates the exchange-rate exposure of fixed yen principal from the interest expense of a replacement loan, following the BIS description of yen-funded carry.

Actual costs depend on the loan and currency hedge.

Japan's two-year government bond yield provides another indication of how investors are pricing the country's monetary policy outlook. A rise in short-term yields alongside a strengthening yen following Friday's inflation report would signal mounting pressure on yen-funded positions.

Conversely, softer inflation could temper expectations of accelerated BOJ tightening, easing one potential source of selling pressure on Bitcoin.

According to recent reports, the immediate risk is that a hotter inflation reading could renew pressure on Bitcoin's fragile recovery while US spot ETF trading remains suspended. Those funds will reopen at 9:30 a.m. ET on Friday, approximately 15 hours after Tokyo's inflation release, leaving Bitcoin's continuously operating global markets to absorb the initial reaction.

In a recent development, back in the day, a sweatsuit was all about comfort. It wasn’t so much a fashion staple, but the kind of thing to throw on and lounge in. With Y2K style back in vogue, matching sweatsuits are more commonplace than ever—just with a little less sparkle than the ones previously sported by icons like Paris Hilton and J.Lo in the early 2000s. And, with the rise of athleisure, these simple sweats have gotten the luxury treatment: they’re softer, more flattering, and pricier than ever.

Whether you’re the kind of person who considers it a cozy wardrobe essential, or you’re just looking to treat yourself to something comfortable to wear around the house, there have never been more choices when it comes to the best matching sweatsuits. Since we’re heading into winter (and Black Friday is just around the corner!), Women’s Health editors tested the most popular styles.

Here are our thoughts on the matching sets after months of lounging in them, working from home in them, and even wearing them to work.

Oner Active Foundations Zip Up Hoodie.

Oner Active Foundations Sweatpants.

In a recent development, oner Active’s workout clothes have had our hearts at WH for a while. That’s why we were excited to put their loungewear to the test. Associate Health and Fitness editor Addison Aloian wore this set while traveling, chilling at home, and even working behind the scenes on a photoshoot.

It has been revealed that “I absolutely love this set from Oner,” she says. She loves it for its comfort, warmth, and versatility (Aloian says she knows she could wear it outside in the chilly NYC winter, layer it under her ski clothes, or pop it on over leggings for her warm-up at the gym). “But the standout feature is the color,” Aloian says. “So many sweat sets are gray or black, but the turquoise is stunning and makes it a standout in my closet when I want a monochromatic moment.” She opted for the “oil blue” color, but Oner also has options like alpine green and toasted red, plus your neutral staples.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also one of the more affordable options we tested—and on sale for half off this Black Friday. But that doesn’t mean it skimps on quality: The material feels super plush since it’s made from 67% cotton and 33% polyester, for a super plush feel that doesn’t pill or shed after one wash.

It has been revealed that the set’s one flaw? The bottoms are a little long. At 5 '1, Aloian indicates she’d love a “short” option as well. Oner does offer a “long” length, though, for the taller girlies.

Old Navy Bounce Fleece Half-Zip Pullover Sweatshirt.

Old Navy High-Waisted Bounce Fleece Jogger Sweatpants.

In a world of expensive sweat sets, Old Navy’s Bounce Fleece line provides a budget-friendly—and stylish—option. “You’d never know these are super affordable,” states Fitness editor Cori Ritchey. They hold their own with the rest of the pricier sets from their fit to their feel.

It has been revealed that the highlight for Ritchey is the material, a mix of polyester, rayon, and spandex. “It moves with you, and the fabric feels like it breathes compared to other sweatsuits that feel too heavy and hot.” One small caveat: Be sure to follow the wash instructions and keep your cycle on cold and gentle, tumble dry low, and keep the garments inside out. Ritchey states she noticed a bit of pilling after the first wash, but says that after following the wash instructions during the next few washes, the set stayed in great shape.

In a recent development, the half-zip and jogger combo makes for a put-together look and is cozy enough for traveling, running errands, or lounging around the house, Ritchey says. The set comes in plenty of neutral colors, plus some fun ones like orchid. It’s also the first on our list that doesn’t have a prominent logo, for anyone who wants a clean-looking set with no branding. Another point for Old Navy: It’s the most size-inclusive on the list. Sizing goes from XS to 4XL, with regular, tall, and petite options.

Alo Accolade Crew Neck Pullover.

Alo is another longtime favorite at WH. The brand is known for its cozy, stylish (and premium-priced) loungewear. The fit is what we love most. The set, which comes in over a dozen colors, has an oversized feel, yet still manages to look intentional, says Deputy Features editor Carina Hsieh. “Unlike other sweatsuits, this one doesn’t look or feel unflattering or sloppy,” she says. She especially likes how it falls on her shoulders.

It’s also the “perfect transition-weather sweatsuit.” The French terry material is made up of 65% cotton and 35% polyester, for a “really soft, thick, and high-quality” feel. The fabric doesn’t feel ultra-heavy, though, so it’s a great pick for fall and spring when you might overheat in thicker sets. Another perk? The pants have pockets.

Sources indicate that however, the sizing isn’t the most intuitive. Hsieh, who is typically a small or medium in other brands, is an extra-extra small in these pants. The pants also run a bit long. Hsieh says sizing down is likely the way to go for this set.

Aritzia Cozy Sweatfleece Mega Funnel Neck.

Aritzia Cozy Sweatfleece Mega Jogger.

I had been hearing great things about Aritzia’s Sweatfleece line, and after testing for over a month, I can attest that it’s truly the coziest sweat set I’ve worn. Made from 78% cotton and 22% polyester, the material is soft with a fleece-lined interior. They’ll definitely keep you warm; that fleece inside is perfect for chilly temps. But they don’t feel too heavy. The material is still breathable, and I don’t get overheated when I’m wearing them.

Industry observers note that I also love the look of this set, especially with the funnel/mockneck style—which is very on-trend. I have been wearing the suit when I work from home, and it makes me feel put together and chic, even though I’m in the coziest clothes I own. I’m also a runner, and I've noticed that this is the first thing I want to put on after I shower post-run. It’s the ultimate comfy outfit for recovery.

According to recent reports, when it comes to sizing, these sweats have a “mega” fit, which means they’re oversized. I still sized up just to make sure mine would be roomy, but learned that I didn’t need to. These give you an oversized fit at your true size. Plus, as a shorter girlie (5’2!), I was thrilled that they came in short, regular, and long lengths. They’re still just the tiniest bit long, so I flip the elastic on each ankle under to shorten the legs. You can’t tell a thing!

Set Active Staple SET Uniform Layered Crewneck.

Set Active Staple Straight Leg Sweatpants.

This vintage-inspired sweatsuit from Set Active is made from 100% cotton, for those who want to prioritize more natural fibers. “I love how soft they feel,” Hsieh notes. “Sometimes 100% cotton feels stiff to me, and I’ve found that cotton sweats in particular lay weirdly at the chest when they’re oversized, but these maintain their plushy softness.”.

This set is mid-weight, cozy, and warm. “I love a crewneck and sweatpants to sleep in, but sometimes find other sweats to be too much underneath my many layers of comforter and other blankets. These are the perfect weight to be warm and let me sleep comfortably,” Hsieh indicates. The crewneck isn't too bulky either—a challenge for a lot of sweatshirts—and fits easily underneath a jacket.

This set comes in tons of bold colorways, with contrasting collars and retro logos on the crewneck—so it’s great for anybody who's into the vintage activewear look. The only con? Hsieh, who is 5’3, found that pants run slightly long.

lululemon Scuba Oversized Full-Zip Hoodie.

lululemon Scuba Mid-Rise Wide-Leg Pant.

This lululemon hoodie was named the best zip-up in our guide to the best hoodies for its comfy, classic fit. Where the hoodie shines, according to Associate Style & Commerce Editor Shannen Zitz, the pants are just as impressive. Both stand out for the waffle material: A soft, stretchy blend of cotton, modal, and polyester. She finds it more breathable than some of her buttery-smooth cotton sweats. Another perk? It’s basically immune to pilling.

“Both pieces are incredibly soft and cozy,” Zitz indicates. “I love the slightly oversized, waist-length fit of the top. It pairs really well with the matching sweatpants, which are equally comfy and have a flattering drape with a straight-leg fit.”.

Sources indicate that this set styled with a plain white tee underneath and a pair of comfortable sneakers “happens to be my travel fit of choice,” she notes. “The hoodie keeps me warm and cozy during cold flights and early morning departure days, but I can easily unzip it or tie it around my waist if I get too warm.”.

Vuori Restore Straight Leg Sweatpant.

According to recent reports, the Restore hoodie is one of Vuori’s best sellers, and for good reason. “I love the material,” Richey indicates. “It’s very soft and feels super durable.” The French terry material (a cotton blend that’s smooth on the outside with brushed fleece on the inside)is made of breathable cotton and sturdy polyester.

Recent findings suggest that as far as sweat sets go, this one has a lot of heft. The Restore line is thicker and denser than the label's BlissBlend or DreamKnit lines, making this set incredibly warm with a high-quality, structured feel. “The softness seems to also stay wash after wash, which is a huge win!” Richey adds.

Sources indicate that when it comes to fit, the hoodie has a perfectly oversized shape, but you might benefit from sizing up in the bottoms, particularly if you’re thicker-thighed, Ritchey notes. The pant comes in short, regular, and long lengths, giving you even more options to find the right fit.

In a recent development, this Spanx set stands out as a lighter-weight and more polished option. “This set feels so light and airy,” claims Zitz. Spanx’s Air Essentials is made of their signature Spacer Fabric (a blend of modal, polyester, and elastane), for an ultra-smooth feel with plenty of stretch.

“It’s one of the most comfortable lounge sets I own, but also one of the nicest looking,” Zitz states. The structured half-zip top and tailored (yet roomy) wide-leg pant have an almost dressed-up look, so you can wear the set to lounge or out of the house. It also comes in nearly 20 colors—a range of neutrals to bright options like red, blue, and plum.

Industry observers note that there is one downside: Neither the top nor bottom has pockets. While they might take away from the streamlined look, being able to slip your phone or wallet into a small pocket would be a bonus.

Gap VintageSoft Oversized Henley Pullover.

Gap VintageSoft Baggy Wide-Leg Sweatpants.

Recent findings suggest that gap certainly holds its own in the loungewear category. Aside from the cozy feel (thanks to a blend of cotton and polyester), it really shines when it comes to style.

In a recent development, “I love a wide-leg sweatpant,” Zitz says. “I find they look less loungey than a jogger, and this pair is roomy without swallowing up my entire frame.” Even better is the henley top: The button-up design and mock neck make this top look more chic than your average crewneck or half-zip. “It’s unlike any other sweatshirt I own in terms of style,” Zitz says.

Recent findings suggest that one area for improvement: The color options. Our tester opted for a soft blue color, but would have preferred a more neutral gray—it just wasn’t in stock due to the limited colorways.

Rhone DreamGlow Barrel Leg Pant.

Rhone is another label that the WH fitness and style editors love. I have personally been a fan of their DreamGlow line for a while. It’s warm, but also has a sleek feel to it. There’s no heaviness to this set at all.

Made primarily of polyester and a small amount of elastane, the fabric also contains lyocell, a semi-synthetic fiber that helps to wick moisture away from the body, creating a slightly cooling effect. This set is ideal for anyone who runs hot or for transitional spring or fall weather. I like to wear it around my apartment on work-from-home days or as a travel outfit.

This is also the set for someone who is a little sweatsuit-reluctant. The top has a slightly cropped and boxy fit, while the pants are a barrel-leg shape (a.k.a. a flared mid-leg and tapered ankle). Combined with the ultra-smooth material, this set looks less frumpy than your old-school sweat suits.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An AI-assisted search of NASA's archived telescope data has uncovered two possible planets, with preliminary checks by a professional astronomer recovering both signals.
  • 24 report, OpenAI detailed how two amateur astronomers used its Codex and Astra tools to search observations of millions of stars for previously overlooked planetary candidates.
  • Kevin Bond, an OpenAI engineer, used Codex to develop software that detects recurring declines in stellar brightness, a potential indication of a planet passing in front of its host star.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An AI-assisted search of NASA's archived telescope data has uncovered two possible planets, with preliminary checks by a professional astronomer recovering both signals.

In a Nov. 24 report, OpenAI detailed how two amateur astronomers used its Codex and Astra tools to search observations of millions of stars for previously overlooked planetary candidates.

Kevin Bond, an OpenAI engineer, used Codex to develop software that detects recurring declines in stellar brightness, a potential indication of a planet passing in front of its host star.

Sources indicate that bond combined existing detection methods into a program that deployed two AI agents. One identified promising signals, while the other subjected those findings to further examination.

Running the software against archived observations of approximately 100,000 stars from NASA's Kepler Space Telescope produced more than 200 signals, including 10 associated with previously confirmed planets.

Vishal Gajjar, an astronomer at the SETI Institute, independently recovered two of Bond's findings.

Recent findings suggest that the first involved a relatively cool star, KIC 5689121, whose brightness declined every 13.8 days. OpenAI remarked the signal was consistent with a potential planet approximately 2.4 times Earth's diameter. The second, KIC 6691030, exhibited recurring dips every 4.8 days, suggesting a potential planet smaller than Neptune.

OpenAI says SETI Institute astronomer Vishal Gajjar recovered both dips in the same Kepler data Kevin Bond searched.

Each repeat interval gives astronomers a pattern to test in follow-up observations.

The traces illustrate timing with schematic dip shapes and depths. The causes of both dips remain unresolved.

According to recent reports, both traces use a common 28.5-day window from an arbitrary starting point. Their dips are spaced at OpenAI’s reported approximate intervals of 13.8 and 4.8 days. Positions are rounded to the nearest SVG coordinate.

Industry observers note that the traces illustrate timing with schematic dip shapes and depths. The causes of both dips remain unresolved.

“Our initial checks are encouraging, and follow-up observations will tell us more.”.

While Bond focused on Kepler's archived observations, another amateur astronomer, Ethan Byrd, used OpenAI's Astra to examine telescope data covering approximately 19 million stars.

Byrd developed two searches, including one targeting planetary candidates within habitable zones, where atmospheric conditions could allow liquid water to exist on a planet's surface.

It has been revealed that his initial search identified 49 candidates. Byrd has submitted one to researchers working on NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission, and two others are awaiting submission.

According to recent reports, astronomers have used artificial intelligence to identify planets for years. In 2017, NASA announced the discovery of Kepler-90i using a neural network trained to recognize planetary signals in telescope observations.

General-purpose AI tools now let amateur astronomers develop their own detection software and search vast archives for signals earlier searches may have missed.

However, recurring declines in stellar brightness can also result from eclipsing stars or fluctuations in telescope instruments.

Astronomers could investigate Bond's candidates by observing their host stars at the predicted transit intervals and measuring whether gravitational forces from potential orbiting planets cause detectable stellar movement.

Establishing whether either signal represents an undiscovered planet could take months or years, OpenAI stated.

A racerback style bra, the style in which the straps meet at the back to create an X or Y shape, happens to be a sort of Goldilocks bra option that suits most sizes because they’re super customizable. As a style writer who’s tested more bras than I can count (at different weights and sizes over the years), I’ve found that racerback sports bras tend to work especially well for smaller and larger busts alike. That’s part of why racerback bras have such a loyal following: they’re supportive, comfortable, less likely to slip around, and easy to style under a variety of workout tops.

This is especially true for bras with added features like underwire, molded cups, or a wider band, says Dani Read, a senior designer for luxury lingerie brand Cosabella. Adjustable straps (as opposed to fixed backs) can also help you get the right fit in a racerback, she adds. Racerback bras are a go-to style for Women’s Health’s style and fitness team, and for this guide, we’ve selected some of our favorites that we reach for again and again.

“My boobs lean on the larger side, so I usually go for sports bras with a higher neckline to keep everything secure (no one wants spillage mid-workout!),” claims style contributor Lily Wohlner. “So when I first got this bra, I was a little skeptical.” She wasn’t sure it would 1) hold her chest up during workouts and 2) provide enough coverage. But Wohlner was pleasantly surprised and found that it actually offers a solid amount of compression, thanks to the nylon and elastane blend, which lifts and supports without feeling flimsy.

It’s become one of her favorite racerback sports bras and she’s consistently impressed by how well it holds her in during strength training classes. The cute, strappy back design definitely doesn’t hurt, either.

Recent findings suggest that another bonus: the fabric dries super rapidly, so even when you break a sweat, you don’t have to worry about visible marks. It feels light and breathable, but the support is legit—like what you’d expect from a more heavy-duty bra. One thing to note: it runs a little major in the chest area. Wohlner says she probably should’ve sized down for a more snug fit. That stated, her usual medium still works, it just doesn’t have that extra-tight, compressive feel some of her high-impact bras do. We also wish it had adjustable straps for customizability.

According to recent reports, crz Yoga makes some of the best workout clothes on Amazon we’ve tested—and the Butterluxe Racerback Sports Bra might just be the softest thing you’ll ever put on your body. Crafted from a luxurious blend of 81 percent polyamide and 19 percent lycra elastane, the signature Butterluxe fabric lives up to its name—smooth and silky. It’s perfect for low-impact workouts like yoga, barre, or stretching, and doubles as a comfy everyday bra you'll actually want to keep on.

If you have a bigger chest, you’ll probably want to layer a sports bra underneath. But if you're part of the itty bitty titty committee, you're good to go wearing this solo pretty much anywhere.

Just a heads-up: it runs small, so consider sizing up if you prefer a less snug fit. That said, I actually don’t mind the tighter feel when I’m in the mood for extra support.

If you’re after a racerback bra that will support you through any move, the On Performance Flex Bra deserves a spot in your drawer. Designed with soft, breathable materials that have compression, this bra is perfect for high-impact workouts like running, boxing, and HIIT.

According to recent reports, the Performance Flex Bra is made with a buttery-soft blend of recycled polyamide and elastane, offering a nice hug that moves with you. It has that sleek racerback cut with no underwires or fastening that allows for full range of motion without digging in. Plus, it features a supportive underband and molded cups (removable!) that give you shape without feeling bulky. Industry observers note that this bra is made with a polyamide and elastane blend, which is soft, breathable, and stretchy. Our experts say that the most important consideration in selecting any type of bra—racerback or otherwise—is finding the right size. And, unfortunately, sometimes you may not be able to find your size at any old retailer. Most stores only stock "standard sizes"—that is, sizes 32-38 B-D, notes Laura Burke, intimate apparel stylist and certified bra fit expert. But inclusive bra sizes go as large as an N cup, she says, so keep an eye out for a wider range of sizes when you're shopping if you need to. And remember: You may have to visit a bra boutique to find sizes on the far end of the spectrum.

In a recent development, when it comes to racerback styles, Read recommends adjustable straps, particularly if you're larger-chested and know you need more support. "The strap placement should have the straps sitting comfortably on your shoulders," she says. The correct strap placement helps alleviate pressure on the shoulders and distribute the weight of your bust evenly, preventing back pain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Walmart is allowing shoppers to purchase Black Friday deals through Meta’s AI assistant Muse without sharing their saved card details.

The retailer unveiled the integration on Nov. 24, expanding its Agent Gateway to allow customers to discover products, build shopping carts, and complete purchases through conversations with Meta’s AI assistant.

Sources indicate that shoppers can ask Muse to find television deals, identify discounted products available for delivery or recommend items based on their preferences. Walmart handles product discovery and checkout through its Gateway, which connects external AI assistants to the retailer’s shopping infrastructure.

To make purchases, shoppers must link their Walmart accounts through a sign-in process that redirects them to the retailer before returning them to Muse.

When adding an item to their cart for the first time, shoppers establish an Agent Profile within their Walmart account and set a spending limit for the assistant.

The profile allows customers to distinguish AI-assisted purchases from other orders in their purchase history. They can also revoke the assistant’s purchasing authority by deleting the profile.

Industry observers note that walmart retains control of payment processing. Under its Agentic Access Terms, only shoppers can designate which saved payment method an AI assistant can use. External agents cannot add cards, change payment preferences or access raw card details, including full card numbers.

It has been revealed that instead, each transaction requires a short-lived authorization token tied to the merchant, shopping cart, purchase amount and session. The token expires upon use, requiring fresh authorization for subsequent transactions.

Recent findings suggest that walmart matches requests from Muse. The shopper manages spending and payment permissions in their Walmart account.

Shoppers check out inside Muse with a saved Walmart card. Walmart claims outside agents receive no raw saved card details.

Sources indicate that walmart’s announcement leaves the exact Muse approval prompts and eligible locations and devices unspecified. The diagram depicts responsibilities and the shopping request.

The illustration indicates the shopping request and the shopper’s account controls described by Walmart in the November Muse walkthrough and the payment provisions in its Gateway terms.

Industry observers note that walmart’s announcement leaves the exact Muse approval prompts and eligible locations and devices unspecified. The diagram depicts responsibilities and the shopping request.

The integration builds on Walmart’s Agent Profiles, introduced in October as part of its efforts to give customers greater control over purchases made through AI assistants.

It has been revealed that by default, shoppers must approve purchases initiated by an agent. However, they can authorize assistants to complete transactions independently within a predetermined spending limit.

It has been revealed that walmart can still request additional confirmation even when a purchase falls within that limit. Its terms also allow the retailer to intervene when transactions exceed or conflict with a customer’s purchasing preferences.

The arrangement creates a framework for AI assistants to move beyond product recommendations and execute purchases on behalf of consumers without directly controlling their payment credentials.

However, Walmart’s launch announcement did not specify when shoppers using Muse would encounter additional approval requests after granting an assistant purchasing authority.

The retailer looks to extend its Gateway to more applications and AI assistants, potentially expanding the number of platforms through which customers can authorize purchases.

Walmart’s existing return policy applies to purchases completed through Muse, although the tech giant has yet to specify which locations and devices are eligible for the rollout.

This high-tech Huawei home battery pack hopes to hold back Tesla’s latest Powerwall with silicon carbide technology, AI-powered energy management baked in, and enough modular storage to keep even large homes bright and warm when the rest of the block goes dark.

In a recent development, huawei believes its latest Luterra S2 is more than just a home backup battery. The Chinese tech firm is calling it an “all-in-one residential energy system” that combines a hybrid inverter, modular battery storage, and AI-powered energy management in a single, simple, and stackable package that’s available in single-phase versions that put out between 3 and 10 kW and three-phase versions that can push up to 20 kW.

The Luterra S2 is the first system of its kind to use Huawei’s proprietary full-silicon carbide (SiC) architecture, which promises improved efficiency, power density, and ease of use. It’s so easy, in fact, that Huawei claims it can be installed and commissioned in just minutes.

According to recent reports, “We are thrilled to introduce Huawei Luterra S2, our next-generation all-in-one residential energy system,” said Steve Zhang, President of Huawei Distributed PV & BESS Business. “By combining full-SiC architecture, AI-driven energy management, and industry-leading safety, Luterra S2 is designed to be smaller, lighter, quieter, safer, smarter and more powerful than ever before.”.

Huawei’s basic Luterra S2 configuration starts with “just” 5 kWh of battery energy storage and 3 kW of output. That’s enough to keep essential household appliances, lighting, and electronics running during a power outage, but you’ll want to keep going if you’re preparing for more than a day or two without power.

If that sounds like you, Luterra’s got you covered. The modular system can be expanded with modular 7 kWh LFP battery packs and can scaling up to a massive 336 kWh of total storage across interconnected systems, with inverter output peaking at an impressive 60 kW using three 20 kW units in parallel.

In a recent development, keeping all that power cool and quiet is a Huawei-developed passive cooling system that does without external fans, keeping operating noise levels below a claimed 29 dB (about the same as my Mac mini). It operates at ambient temperatures from –25° C to about 60° C, and features a sturdy IP66-rated enclosure (safe to hit with a high-pressure hose) with corrosion protection up to C5-M to keep it from rusting away.

Nice, but no mention of price or European availability.

Sources indicate that alas, the Luterra S2 probably won’t be making its way to the US anytime soon – but fear not! Tech Report: Bitcoin’s $60,000 recovery masks a growing threat that could push its price as low as $29,000

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that bitcoin recovered above $60,000 after slipping below that mark on Nov.
  • BTC rebounded to $63,000 on Monday, but subsequently surrendered much of those gains.
  • It has been revealed that according to Talos, Bitcoin lost 7.9% over the week, compared with declines of 2.9% for the S&P 500, 4.5% for the Nasdaq 100 and 7.8% for gold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that bitcoin recovered above $60,000 after slipping below that mark on Nov. 25, in a volatile week in which Bitcoin fell to around $55,000, its lowest level since September 2024.

BTC rebounded to $63,000 on Monday, but subsequently surrendered much of those gains.

It has been revealed that according to Talos, Bitcoin lost 7.9% over the week, compared with declines of 2.9% for the S&P 500, 4.5% for the Nasdaq 100 and 7.8% for gold. Over 30 days, Bitcoin has fallen 25.3%, approximately 2.6 times the Nasdaq 100's decline.

Bitcoin's correlation with traditional risk assets has also strengthened. Its 30-day correlations with the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Nvidia climbed to 0.78, 0.77 and 0.68, respectively, roughly 1.4 to twice their one-year medians.

Galaxy Research noted that Bitcoin's recent struggles are particularly unusual given its September recovery above the 50-week moving average, which has historically helped identify the end of bear markets.

Bitcoin has since fallen below both its 50-week and 200-week moving averages, breaking a recovery pattern that had held since 2011.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin reclaimed its 50-week moving average in September after spending 44 consecutive weeks below it. It held above the indicator for seven weeks, reaching a daily close of $86,521 on Oct. 4, nearly 48% above its June low.

Galaxy found that none of the seven previous recoveries that sustained the moving average for at least seven weeks later produced a new bear-market low, even intraday.

September's recovery differed from earlier instances in one significant respect. Previous recoveries after prolonged periods below the moving average followed declines of 76.7% to 92.7%, whereas September's followed a comparatively shallow 53% drawdown on a closing basis.

Sources indicate that bitcoin's subsequent decline to $55,100 on Nov. 21 prompted Galaxy to withdraw its October assessment that the bear market ended in June.

The breakdown shifts attention to Bitcoin's June 30 closing low of $58,525.

Galaxy identified seven completed instances in which Bitcoin closed below a bear market low that had held for at least 60 days and from which the cryptocurrency had rebounded at least 20%.

Industry observers note that all seven resulted in further declines of at least 17.1%, with a median loss of 51.8%. Applied to Bitcoin's June closing low, those historical outcomes would put the cryptocurrency at approximately $48,500 and $28,200, respectively.

However, another closing low would push Bitcoin beyond the historical duration of its bear markets.

In a recent development, as of Nov. 22, 412 days had elapsed since Bitcoin reached its record closing price of $124,824 in October 2025. Its four previous bear markets took between 163 and 406 days to bottom.

Recent findings suggest that the current downturn has also exceeded historical halving-to-bottom timelines. The three previous cycle lows occurred between 777 and 912 days after their respective halvings, compared with the 946 days since Bitcoin's April 2024 halving.

While those timelines suggest Bitcoin is overdue for a recovery, its valuation and investor behavior point toward an unfinished bear market.

Bitcoin's previous four bear markets recorded peak-to-trough closing-price declines of approximately 93%, 85%, 84% and 77%, respectively.

Industry observers note that successive downturns have become shallower, but the largest reduction between previous cycles was eight percentage points. A bottom at the June closing low would represent a 24% reduction.

The divergence extends to Bitcoin's realized price, which estimates the aggregate cost basis of its circulating supply.

According to recent reports, during previous bear markets, Bitcoin spent between 140 and 304 days below its realized price. It has yet to register a single daily close below that level, which stood at $53,205 on Nov. 22.

In a recent development, meanwhile, the proportion of Bitcoin's supply held at a loss reached 57% on Nov. 20, within the 55% to 61% range recorded at previous cycle bottoms.

Despite that financial distress, Bitcoin's 30-day realized losses peaked at just 3.6% of its realized capitalization in February, compared with peaks of 7.3% to 16.7% during previous bear markets.

In a recent development, investor sentiment has deteriorated more sharply. Galaxy's proprietary Bitcoin Fear & Greed Index fell to 5.2 on Nov. 21, its lowest reading since June 2022 and among the lowest 0.5% of historical readings.

Yet the index has spent just six days at or below 10 during the current downturn, compared with between 12 and 57 days during previous bear markets, including the month following their bottoms.

Sources indicate that derivatives traders have also maintained relatively resilient positioning. Bitcoin perpetual futures funding averaged a positive annualized rate of 4.3% over the seven days through Nov. 22, compared with negative 24.5% shortly after the November 2022 bottom.

It has been revealed that as of Nov. 22, Bitcoin satisfied just two of the 13 historical bottom indicators Galaxy tracks.

The conflict between BTC's historical cycle duration and the depth of its losses leaves Galaxy examining two potential scenarios.

Industry News: Check your ego at the door: Stellantis’ new electric dolly turns ANY car into a tow rig

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ upcoming patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.
  • In a recent development, originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No.
  • In other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a substantial tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ upcoming patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.

In a recent development, originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No. 12,779,916 for its electric tow dolly on 03NOV2026. The patent covers a machine that’s designed to shoulder the trailer’s hitch load with its own ball hitch or fifth-wheel plate, using an on-board electric motor and battery to get the trailer going while its regenerative braking system and AI-backed steering and traction control system keeps everything pointed in the right direction.

In other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a substantial tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction. The vehicle up front doesn’t necessarily need a massive motor, heavy-duty suspension or oversized brakes. With a system like this, you could argue that the “tow vehicle” isn’t really a tow vehicle at all. It’s more of a “lead vehicle,” since the dolly is the one doing the towing … and it can follow just about anything – including the diminutive (and supremely affordable) Fiat 500e, which is also made by Stellantis.

To be clear, this isn’t just Uncle Jojo making fun of the commuter conveys – Stellantis’ patent describes the dolly as being equipped with an autonomous control system using cameras, sensors, a controller, and an advanced, four wheel steer-by-wire system. It also specifically discusses how the dolly’s independently powered acceleration, braking and steering, and sway controls essentially remove the need to own a truck in the first place.

The dolly system’s truck bed sides and small size allow consumers to experience the functionality and utility of a truck only when they need it, allowing them to own a smaller, cheaper, and more fuel efficient vehicle that suits daily use needs.

There are some pretty obvious practical questions still to answer, of course, including how much battery capacity the dolly would need, how much weight it could handle and how it would perform on long grades or in emergency braking situations. And, to be clear, a patent isn’t a product announcement or proof that Stellantis aims to put one of these things on sale – heck, if I were Stellantis’ CEO, I’d patent this thing just to prevent anyone else from building one so I could keep selling ancient, low-tech, high-margin Ram Trucks – but it’s a neat idea.

Recent findings suggest that okay, I like this idea and appreciate the problem it is trying to solve, but it has the same challenge as any electric-tow situation, which is the charging logistics. Even if you find a pull-through charger (very rare), if you are using an EV, you still need to charge two "vehicles," so you have to charge your car, then pull up and charge the dolly afterwards. Even if you are using a gas car, charging the dolly will be logistically challenging. Of course, that's a problem with an easy solution (more pull-through chargers), but also one that doesn't seem to be on any charging network's radar.

I think it’s neat, anyway. What do you guys think? Are you ready to trade in your major-battery Chevy Silverado EV or Volvo VNR 800 on a new Topolino, or are you going to keep driving inefficient 99% of the time? Let us know, in the comments.

SOURCE: Stellantis, via Mopar Insiders.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

So, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.).

And, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

Sources indicate that first: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most crucial things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

It has been revealed that at the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

According to recent reports, keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”.

And, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse notes—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse noted. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”.

It has been revealed that keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse remarked. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training blueprint all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Strategy, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

According to recent reports, age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chainlink's LINK token climbed 10% over the past 24 hours to $9.20 as the network deepened its integration with traditional finance.
  • The rally comes as Fidelity Investments filed to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund (ETF), a day after enabling direct LINK trading on its cryptocurrency platform.
  • Meanwhile, Chainlink has expanded its financial market data infrastructure to support round-the-clock trading and lending involving tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets, including during market holidays such as Thanksgiving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chainlink's LINK token climbed 10% over the past 24 hours to $9.20 as the network deepened its integration with traditional finance.

The rally comes as Fidelity Investments filed to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund (ETF), a day after enabling direct LINK trading on its cryptocurrency platform.

Meanwhile, Chainlink has expanded its financial market data infrastructure to support round-the-clock trading and lending involving tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets, including during market holidays such as Thanksgiving.

On Nov. 25, Fidelity submitted a registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for its proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, which would trade on Nasdaq under the ticker FLNK.

Recent findings suggest that the fund would hold LINK directly, with Anchorage Digital, BitGo and Coinbase Custody safeguarding its assets. It would support cash and in-kind share creations and redemptions but would not stake its underlying tokens.

The filing came a day after Fidelity added LINK, AAVE and UNI to its Fidelity Crypto platform, expanding its customers' access to digital assets.

While eligible Fidelity Crypto customers can now purchase LINK directly, the proposed ETF would extend that access to investors seeking exposure through conventional brokerage accounts.

It has been revealed that the consecutive moves could substantially broaden LINK's investor base. Fidelity serves approximately 57 million individual investors and reported $7.9 trillion in managed assets and $20.1 trillion in assets under administration at the end of September, making it one of the largest financial services firms in the US.

However, Fidelity is entering a market where investor appetite has weakened considerably.

According to recent reports, according to SoSoValue data, Grayscale and Bitwise's spot Chainlink ETFs have attracted $176 million in cumulative net inflows since their respective launches. However, the funds recorded net inflows for just one day in November, putting them on course for their first month of net withdrawals since the market's inception.

Sources indicate that daily net flows for GLNK and CLNK through Nov. 25. Values follow Maketo's displayed rounding and totals are approximate, and non-trading days are excluded.

Source: Maketo Chainlink ETF daily flows.

The slowdown in demand, coupled with LINK's price decline, has reduced the funds' combined net assets by approximately 33%, from $238.2 million at the end of September to $158.6 million on Nov. 25.

Fidelity's extensive retail and financial advisory network could help revive demand, but limited fresh capital could also intensify competition among issuers.

With Fidelity yet to disclose its management fee or launch date, the terms of its offering could determine how effectively it competes with Grayscale and Bitwise for LINK investors.

Beyond expanding investment access to LINK, Chainlink is positioning its infrastructure to capture growing demand for financial markets that operate outside traditional exchange hours.

On Nov. 26, the decentralized oracle network introduced Chainlink 24/7 on its X account, a market data service that extends pricing coverage for traditional financial assets to weekends and public holidays.

The service builds on Chainlink's existing 24/5 infrastructure, which provides pricing for more than $1.6 billion in tokenized equities across six blockchains and supports platforms including Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, and Coinbase.

Previously, blockchain-based financial applications struggled to value traditional assets when their underlying markets closed, limiting trading opportunities and complicating collateral management.

Chainlink's latest service addresses that gap by combining traditional market data during active trading sessions with perpetual-futures-derived pricing when exchanges are closed.

The infrastructure could support continuous trading in tokenized assets, derivatives, and prediction markets, while letting decentralized lending protocols manage collateral risks outside conventional market hours.

Aave, which had more than $34 billion in total value locked at the service's launch, is adopting the infrastructure through Horizon, its institutional lending platform, initially targeting tokenized US equities.

The expansion also affects LINK's economics.

Fidelity's ETF prospectus identifies demand for Chainlink's services as a factor influencing LINK's value, noting that the network converts certain fees paid in fiat currencies and other digital assets into LINK through its Payment Abstraction mechanism.

While Fidelity's expansion creates another avenue for investment demand, Chainlink's ability to generate additional fee-paying activity from always-on financial markets could provide a separate source of demand for its token.

Recent findings suggest that layerZero describes a 1% annual issuance target as the basis for the reward pool, and the terms set an initial validator commission of 10% on rewards. A holder’s share depends on how much ZRO they stake, how long they stake it, and how much others commit.

Any rewards compound into the locked position, and the staking guide states validators will set their own commission after the initial period.

#145715. Breaking: Why Sleep Consistency May Be the Missing Piece When It Comes to Heart Health

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1759 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Why Sleep Consistency May Be the Missing Piece When It Comes to Heart Health

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You probably already know that getting seven to nine hours of sleep each night is one of the best things you can do for your health and wellbeing.
  • It has been revealed that as it turns out, your heart might not be too happy about that.
  • In a recent development, before you start stressing over every late night or weekend sleep-in, though, there's some notable context to understand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You probably already know that getting seven to nine hours of sleep each night is one of the best things you can do for your health and wellbeing. But what happens if you’re consistently hitting that goal while going to bed at different times? Think 10 p.m. on Monday, midnight on Wednesday, and well past 1 a.m. on Saturday because it’s the weekend, after all.

It has been revealed that as it turns out, your heart might not be too happy about that. Latest research suggests that sleep consistency—which includes both when you go to bed and wake up, and how much sleep you get from night to night—could play an important role in cardiovascular health. And, while getting the recommended amount of shut-eye still matters, researchers are finding that how much your sleep fluctuates may deserve some attention, too.

In a recent development, before you start stressing over every late night or weekend sleep-in, though, there's some notable context to understand. Here's what the research actually found, why your body seems to care so much about routine, and how consistent your sleep schedule really needs to be.

Industry observers note that meet the experts: Nguyen Minh Tuan Viet, MD, PhD, is a neuroscientist and postdoctoral research fellow at Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School and lead researcher of the new study. Nour Makarem, PhD, is a cardiovascular epidemiologist in the department of epidemiology at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health. Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, is a professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center.

For the newly introduced study published in Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, researchers analyzed more than one million nights of sleep data from 10,362 adults participating in the National Institutes of Health's All of Us Research Program, an initiative that aims to collect data from over one million Americans and create the country’s largest biomedical database.

Sources indicate that unlike previous studies that only looked at people's sleep habits for about a week, this one used about six months of Fitbit data to see how participants' bedtimes, wake-up times, and total sleep duration changed from night to night. They then compared those patterns with participants’ medical records and tracked their health for nearly four years.

It has been revealed that the findings were pretty eye-opening: For every additional 29 minutes of variation in how long someone slept from night to night, their relative risk of serious heart problems, including heart attacks, heart failure, heart muscle disease, and certain strokes, was 24 percent higher. To be clear, that doesn't mean going to bed 29 minutes later than usual on a given night increases your heart disease risk by 24 percent. The researchers were looking at a statistical measure of how much someone's total sleep duration varied over time, rather than the consequences of one late bedtime. As of now, all this information does it point to a potential link between sleep schedule variation and heart disease.

Sources indicate that researchers also found that greater night-to-night fluctuations in bedtime and wake-up times were associated with a 23 percent and 20 percent higher relative risk of cardiovascular problems, respectively. This means that both the consistency of your sleep schedule and the consistency of the duration of that sleep may play a role in heart health.

Industry observers note that there are a few things worth keeping in mind, though. For starters, this study found a connection between inconsistent sleep and heart problems, but it couldn't prove that irregular sleep is what causes those problems. In fact, Viet points out that the relationship could work in the opposite direction too (i.e. early illness might actually make someone’s sleep more irregular). Plus, most participants were women and white, so we can't necessarily assume the findings apply to everyone. Still, the results add to growing evidence that sleep consistency deserves a place in the heart-health conversation.

In a recent development, your body has its own internal clock, known as your circadian rhythm, which determines when you're tired, when you're wide awake, and even how bodily functions like blood pressure and heart rate change throughout the day. And, it works at its best when it has a reasonably predictable schedule to follow. When you're constantly changing when you sleep and wake, you may disrupt that rhythm, a phenomenon known as circadian misalignment, explains Nour Makarem, PhD, a cardiovascular epidemiologist in the department of epidemiology at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health.

Sources indicate that that disruption can impact some pretty vital cardiovascular processes, like how your body regulates blood pressure. Under normal circumstances, blood pressure usually drops by about 10 to 20 percent while you're sleeping to give your cardiovascular system a period of rest, but research by Makarem suggests that irregular sleep patterns may be associated with higher blood pressure and an increased risk of hypertension. “This is problematic because higher nocturnal blood pressure and having a non-dipping profile (blood pressure that does not dip or dip enough during sleep) are associated with higher risk for heart disease and stroke, the leading causes of death in women,” she indicates.

Recent findings suggest that your sleep schedule may also interact with other daily rhythms, including when you eat and exercise. These behaviors help regulate biological clocks throughout your body, including those involved in metabolism, Makarem states. When those clocks fall out of sync, processes like blood sugar regulation may be affected, too. In fact, research has linked irregular sleep patterns with poorer glucose regulation and a higher risk of metabolic complications.

It has been revealed that research is still emerging, but scientists are noticing some important links between sleep consistency and heart health. A 2025 study published in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health followed more than 72,000 adults and found that people with irregular sleep patterns had a higher risk of major cardiovascular events, including heart attacks and strokes. Another study published in Sleep in 2024 analyzed sleep patterns in more than 60,000 adults and found that sleep regularity was a stronger predictor of mortality risk than sleep duration in that population.

Industry observers note that so, does this mean having a consistent bed and rising time matters more than getting eight hours? Not necessarily. "The evidence for sleep regularity is rather nascent relative to that for sleep duration," notes Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, a professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. She explains that while several studies have made the connection between irregular sleep and poorer health outcomes, more research needs to be done to determine whether making someone's sleep schedule more consistent can actually lower their cardiovascular risk. And, we do have plenty of evidence that getting enough sleep has positive affects on just about every system in the body, from brain function to muscle recovery.

Overall, there are still things researchers are learning about sleep consistency and heart health, but it’s safe to start thinking of it as another piece of the puzzle, alongside getting enough hours and making sure those hours are restorative.

Recent findings suggest that here's the million-dollar question: Does protecting your heart mean going to bed at exactly 10:30 p.m. every single night, no exceptions? Thankfully, no.

In a recent development, ultimately, you’ve got some wiggle room. "In general, we would recommend that individuals try not to deviate by 60 min up or down from their average bedtime or sleep duration," says St-Onge, but the smaller the gap, the better.

Think of that as a target, not a hard-and-fast rule. An occasional late night or weekend sleep-in isn’t a reason to panic. What matters more is establishing a reasonably consistent pattern over a period of time rather than expecting yourself to follow a perfect schedule every single night.

If you've had a particularly short night, St-Onge recommends trying to go to bed a little earlier and waking up a little later when your schedule allows, rather than trying to make up for all that lost sleep by sleeping in for hours. Most importantly, don't sweat it. "If one night is off, it's not all doom and gloom; you get right back on schedule the following night," claims St-Onge.

Here are a few small changes experts recommend to improve your sleep routine without completely overhauling your lifestyle.

Before committing to being in bed every night by 9 p.m., consider what will actually make sense for your schedule. Earlier isn't automatically better. What's important is getting adequate sleep on a schedule that works with your body's natural rhythm and everyday responsibilities, explains St-Onge.

Sources indicate that if your current bedtime is midnight but you'd ideally like to be asleep by 11, there's no need to make that change all at once. Makarem recommends gradually shifting your bedtime earlier by about 10 minutes each day until you reach your target. The idea is to give your body time to adjust rather than suddenly expecting yourself to fall asleep an hour earlier than usual.

Industry observers note that it's tempting to stay up late on Friday and Saturday nights and make up for it by sleeping well into the morning, but even those brief changes can leave you feeling out of sync by the time Monday rolls around. If possible, St-Onge recommends keeping your weekend bedtimes within about an hour of your usual routine.

According to recent reports, if you wear an Apple Watch or Fitbit to bed, you know how easy it is to get caught up in the numbers. One morning you're celebrating a great sleep score, and the next you're wondering what went wrong because your tracker says you barely got any deep sleep.

According to recent reports, while these devices can be helpful for spotting patterns, the last thing you want is to start losing sleep over your sleep. Makarem recommends using trackers to keep tabs on your habits or remind you when it's time for bed, but only if they're actually helping. If checking your sleep stats is making you anxious, it's fine to ditch the data and simply pay attention to when you're going to bed and waking up.

And remember, you don't have to get your sleep schedule exactly right every single night to do something good for your heart. Small changes that you can actually stick with are worth more than chasing a perfect score. As Makarem puts it, "Progress is better than perfect.".

In a recent development, for a test of the next day’s order book, CryptoSlate selected the five addresses that led the Nov. 25 session in fills of at least 1,000 XRP, then simulated removing their buy orders.

Funded RLUSD in the first 100 buy offers fell from about 63,925 to 8,805. In the model, the matching pool, a standing reserve of both assets, took most of a 100,000 XRP sale after the removal. A seller would receive about 3.3% less RLUSD than with the full sample.

The last XRP/USD trade on Kraken was $0.94935 when the ticker was checked at 13:07:24 UTC on Nov. 26. On the ledger exchange itself, XRP/RLUSD accounted for 84% of all volume measured in XRP over the seven days covered by XRPL.to’s reconstruction.

In a recent development, in the 24 hours ending at 01:30 UTC on Nov. 25, XRPL.to’s reconstruction counted 25,801 fills moving about 6.3 million XRP. Traders took resting offers from 142 accounts or traded against the automated pool.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest account, whose ledger address starts with rpiFwLYi, supplied 41% of executed volume. Together, the five largest supplied 72%, and the pool accounted for 3%.

A replay through the public trade history endpoint yielded 6.32 million XRP and counted 25,712 fills for the same window, 89 fewer than the published tally.

According to recent reports, the index can group multiple executions into one transaction row. In one row covering 525.58 XRP, the validated transaction showed about 514 tokens went to one account’s buy orders and about 12 tokens to another’s.

To test whether concentration persisted, CryptoSlate used XRPL.to records and split combined fills using validated ledger changes.

The comparison covered same-pair fills of at least 1,000 XRP in three 24-hour windows ending at 01:30 UTC on Nov. 24, 25 and 26. The same five addresses, selected by Nov. 25 qualifying volume, accounted for about 71%, 88%, and 79% of qualifying volume, respectively.

It has been revealed that the address starting with rpiFwLYi led the middle session, with about half the qualifying volume. An address starting with rURtT5MM led the sessions on either side.

That left the same group with a large share in all three windows even as the leading address changed, and the turnover includes trades in which the addresses gave or received XRP.

Recent findings suggest that the two sides of the XRP Ledger’s order book draw on different inventories. A resting order to buy XRP is funded in RLUSD, which the seller receives. A resting order to sell XRP draws on the seller’s inventory.

The relevant depth for a seller is the RLUSD that buyers can deliver at the displayed prices.

At validated ledger 108584374, which closed at 13:09:20 UTC on Nov. 26, the first 100 buy offers could take about 67,549 XRP at the displayed prices.

Excluding buy offers from the five large-fill leaders left room for about 9,302 XRP in that same sample. The funded RLUSD in the sample fell about 86%.

The matching XRP/RLUSD pool held about 1.99 million XRP and 1.89 million RLUSD. The model applied its standard 0.315% fee and allocated each portion of the sale to the better available price.

The test held the remaining offers fixed and used only the sampled book and the direct pool, with deeper orders, replacement orders, and additional fees outside the simulation.

The pool took about 32,451 XRP in the first case and 90,698 after the orders were removed.

Industry News: $20K Nissan NX7 PHEV goes on sale with nearly 200 miles of electric range

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dongfeng Nissan officially opened the early order book on its newly introduced NX7 hybrid yesterday, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a $20,000 price tag.

Recent findings suggest that when the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range. The manufacturer’s latest 2027 Rogue Hybrid is a step in the right direction, using a gas engine to generate electricity for a pair of electric drive motors that deliver a driving experience that’s remarkably similar to a “pure” electric car – but without a plug, it’s still entirely dependent on fossil fuels. The fresh Dongfeng Nissan NX7, though? That’s a different story.

The plug-in hybrid Dongfeng Nissan NX7 might be called a “long range hybrid” in the same sense that Volvo’s Euro-market XC70 is, in that it’s an EV for the 360-odd days a year that you’re driving less than 200 miles, and an ICE vehicle for the handful of days you drive more. And if you’re one of those people who thinks stopping on road trips is a character flaw, a fully charged and topped off NX7 will take you an astonishing 1,666 km (~1,035 miles) from where you started.

The new NX7 could be an ideal lilypad vehicle for North American drivers who are either too afraid of being caught without a charger or too invested in the outcome of one or more dumb oil wars to confidently make the switch to EV – and, even at twice the 129,900 yuan ($~19,400) asking price, I think it would be a hit.

For that money, NX7 buyers get an absolutely loaded Model Y-sized crossover (they’re within 1/4″ of each other in length), with a 17.3″ central touchscreen, a fully digital instrument cluster, and (on higher-spec models) a positively massive 55″ augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor and running on Nissan OS 3.0 with an AI-powered voice assistant developed with iFlytek that, Nissan claims, can recognize natural-language commands, remember user preferences, and even recognize occupants, adjusting vehicle settings accordingly.

Industry observers note that on top-shelf models, the NX7 cabins get “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats that use sensors and air-cushion arrays to dynamically adjust for maximum comfort, and include heating, ventilation, and a 12-point SPA-level massage function. The front seats can be fully reclined to create a bed-like configuration that will be familiar to Cube owners. The NX7 even offers an on-board refrigerator and motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by as much as 83% (which, like, I wouldn’t want to be the one to test that – but seems cool).

Power comes from a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated internal combustion engine making 98 hp that’s paired to a 228 hp electric drive motor and the previously mentioned 40.9 kWh LFP battery. It’s not immediately clear if the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system like a Prius or a series-hybrid-plus-plug setup, but Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe a pretty versatile arrangement with four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation – which means the vehicle can theoretically use the ICE motor as a generator, drive the wheels mechanically, or work alongside the electric motor, depending on what the operating conditions call for. Whether any or all four modes make it to production on the NX7 remains to be seen, but it’s an intriguing bit of engineering for a vehicle promising nearly 200 miles of electric driving range.

Why is this article written like it will be available in the US market? It’s made in China and has Chinese software, we’ll never see it.

The final production version will be shown to the public for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show later this month, but you can let us know what you think of the new NX7 in the comments, today.

SOURCE | IMAGES: Dongfeng Nissan, via CarNewsChina.
